scope: Read-only bounded priority/applicability scout; correctness accepted by separate parent verdicts, not rechecked here.

output.summary: Bounded, read-only check of the primary sources on 2026-10-19. It covers priority and whether published theorems apply, nothing else. Correctness is taken from the four parent verdicts and was not rechecked. Source versions used: Menon arXiv:2608.15873v1, which is the only version (/abs/2608.15873v2 returns HTTP 404, and both the arXiv API and DataCite list v1 only). Margolis–Schnabel (M-S) arXiv:1803.03569v1, the only arXiv version; the journal text (Beitr. Algebra Geom. 60 (2019) 399–418) is paywalled. Zhu arXiv:0807.2207v1. Restated with the lane README definitions [INFERENCE], the accepted complete K6.3 exclusion (K63-U0 + K63-D + K63-E + K63-RES) says: if r_0..r_6 are pairwise coprime and r_0 is odd, then (3r_0, 6r_1, …, 6r_6) is not G-harmonic for any group G. K7 is the family (6r_1, …, 6r_7) with pairwise coprime r_i. No theorem I located excludes either family. Menon Thm 4.2, M-S Prop 4.7 and M-S Lemma 4.6 need two indices of the form 3·odd; K6.3 has one and K7 has none. Deleting cosets and applying Zhu Thm 1.1, M-S Props 4.2/4.3/4.5, Theorem B or Sun(t≤6) gives nothing, because every subfamily with two 6r indices has a pair with gcd 6, and the short subtuples are Z-harmonic. M-S Prop 3.8 and Cor 3.9 exclude only alpha patterns with many alpha=1 entries [INFERENCE]. FG takes the triangle-level bounds of Zhu (3.1), M-S Lemma 3.10 and Menon Prop 4.1 and iterates them over every subset of the six other vertices, with no alpha hypothesis; the result is gcd(n_v, T_Q) | 6 and mu ≥ 1/6. The 5/6 fibre bound enlarges the set left uncovered in the M-S Lemma 3.5 and Prop 4.3 arguments to measure ≥ 1/6. Both are elementary extensions of known tools. I did not find either stated in the sources read, and neither is a new method. For K7-U1, Z23-P5 and D23 I found no earlier equivalent. They do not follow from M-S, Menon or Zhu, nor from the lane's earlier accepted K7 results. None of the four restates X1. What the four results add: the full K6.3 tuple-family exclusion, which is conditional on the internal, computer-assisted Sun(5)/Sun(6); two excluded K7 subfamilies (U1: exactly one marked vertex; Z23-P5: 2- and 3-markers shared on one vertex with the 5-marker elsewhere); and row-pattern exclusions (D23). Full Sun(7) remains OPEN: K7 is open when the 2- and 3-markers sit on different vertices, and K6.2* is open. Calibrated significance: modest extension, not major. No novelty claim (a search miss is not evidence of novelty) and no publication claim.

significance.definition_of_major: Any one of: a new method; a full resolution of a prominent open case (for example Sun(7), or Sun(k) for some k ≥ 5 in arbitrary groups, with imports that can be checked independently); or a quantitative gain over published results under the same assumptions
significance.positive_characterization: Written exclusions, conditional and model-reviewed, of one complete 7-term family of coset indices (K6.3) and of marker-defined K7 subfamilies. They combine the product-set and double-coset counting of Margolis–Schnabel, Zhu and Menon with the lane's weighted fibre rows, coset inversion and the FG granularity bound
material_delta: Complete K6.3, restated [INFERENCE]: (3r_0, 6r_1, …, 6r_6) with pairwise coprime r's and r_0 odd is not G-harmonic for any group. Conditional on the internal, computer-assisted Sun(6) (stated) and Sun(5) [INFERENCE] and on the lane's rule stack. No earlier equivalent was located; it is not a corollary of X1, of coset deletion, or of any Z result

K7 subfamilies: the tuples with exactly one r_i not coprime to 30 (U1), and those with r_z = 2^E·3^A·w_z and r_p = 5^B·w_p (Z23-P5). Together with the accepted M0, M1, Z2 and K7-35, this excludes every K7 tuple in which the 2- and 3-markers share a vertex or one of them is absent

D23: in the family with the 2- and 3-markers on different vertices, both rows at z cannot be 4-type (5-marker anywhere). When the five other vertices are unmarked, neither row can be 4-type. This restricts row patterns only

FG: a lemma about subgroups. If all pairwise products are proper, then gcd(n_v, T_Q) | 6 and mu ≥ 1/6 for the K6.3-residue index shapes, which gives the 5/6 fibre bound. It is a supporting tool, not a stand-alone result

significance.frontier: Full Sun(7) remains OPEN. In K7, the family with the 2- and 3-markers on different vertices is open. D23 removes the 4-type row patterns at z; rows with three or more 3s in both orientations, and mixed rows when the 5-marker is on a third vertex, remain open. K6.2* is open: K62-FG and K62-R2 had not been accepted when I read the directory. No correctness re-check or publication claim is made

counterpoints: A bounded search miss is not novelty. Gong's k = 5 thesis and any unpublished Nanjing work on k = 6 or 7 were not located. CNKI, MathSciNet, zbMATH and Google Scholar were not searched

The K6.3 and K7 index families come straight out of the elementary prime-incidence analysis of a Sun(7) counterexample, so anyone working on k = 7 would meet them. Unpublished overlapping work cannot be ruled out

Against over-dismissal: none of the four is a corollary of coset deletion, of X1 or of a Z result. M-S Prop 3.8 and Cor 3.9 cover only patterns heavy in alpha=1 entries, and FG is not stated in any source read
All four results share one family of methods: LFC/VFC rows, inversion, CROSS/LIGHT and the four-type endings, plus FG for K6.3. They should be presented as one contribution carrying one priority risk

Dependence: the K6.3 completeness uses the internal, computer-assisted Sun(6) (stated) and Sun(5) [INFERENCE]. Only Sun(5) has an external claim, and that claim is unpublished. A defect in either would reopen these results
Correctness rests on written proofs, two CLI model reviews and parent re-derivation, with no Lean or human review. It was not re-checked here
On its own the K6.3 theorem is of limited value: it answers no question posed in the literature located. Its weight comes from being one of the three final Sun(7) classes
Menon's n = 5 counterexamples to Question 1 show that excluding non-Z-harmonic families in arbitrary groups is genuinely group-theoretic. This argues against calling the lane's exclusions trivial
access_holes: The refereed M-S text in BAG is paywalled. Only the landing-page metadata, the abstract and the 13-item reference list were read; the published numbering of Lemmas 3.4, 3.10, 4.6, Props 3.8, 4.7 and Cor 3.9 was not verified

Sun 2006 was read only up to about page 11 (Conjecture 1.2, Remark 1.5, Theorem 2.1)
Gong's bachelor thesis (2009 or 2010) was not located. Huhn–Megyesi 1982, Sun 1992 (Chinese Ann. Math.), Chen 1998, Korec 1974 and Ginosar–Schnabel 2011 were not read; they concern Z or partitions
